end.summary:
Asha practised identifying herbivores, carnivores, and food chains.
Manav gave examples including grass–grasshopper–frog–snake and grass–deer–lion.
They predicted changes when grasshoppers, snakes, mice, or bees are removed.
Teach-back was not passed; the removal-effect prediction was not correct without help.
end.parentNote: Manav practised tracing who eats whom and explaining how removing one living thing can affect the rest of a chain. They used arrows and gave several food-chain examples, including grass–deer–lion and algae–mosquito larvae–fish–kingfisher. Some answers were uncertain, and no later correction of the removal-effect prediction was recorded. At home, ask Manav to draw a three- or four-step food chain and explain what may happen if one part is removed.
